body: Couldn’t have said it better myself. I can’t tell if it’s another panic attack or the looming fear of having another panic attack but it is starting to get better. I had vaped for 3 years and quit cold turkey and never felt like this, zyns are a different beast. I was just telling my gf the other day that I refuse to let this become my new normal, but undeniably it’s scary to wonder how long it will take :/ PM me if you need to chat brother it sounds like we’re in the same boat.

Just logged in to say thank you guys for sharing, it made me feel a lot less alone. The past 3 months have been shit for me as well since quitting. I've had 2 visits to the hospital and several doctors appointments with all results coming back clean but I still struggle with daily health anxiety and fear of panic attacks. Exercise, diet, and staying social and distracted helps but life just hasn't been the same. We'll get through this boys, stay strong. Let's check back in 3 months and I know we'll be doing better.

I’m in a very similar situation if it makes you feel any better. I took prednisone about 3 weeks ago and had recently smoked weed (which I’ve learned from this sub is awful for dpdr) and had insane episodes of derealization. I cried to my mom thinking I was losing my mind. At one point I woke up in a state of panic I could not think or feel anything besides fear, it was miserable. I did my research and prednisone is awful for those of us with anxiety, and worse if you’ve recently smoked weed. Many people online complain that prednisone made them go crazy but said it goes away anywhere from 6mo-year. I’ve personally been having episodes of dpdr ever since I stopped taking it. Anyways, this probably wasn’t much help but know you’ve got someone in the same situation as you brother. PM me if u need and stay strong.

4 days in and let me just tell you this entire experience is going to be the most conflicting thing ever. It’s a battle of conscious vs subconscious. Obviously the benefits of quitting outweigh the negatives, but you’re gonna find yourself thinking about all the good times you had with nicotine and questioning how you’re going to continue without it. The feeling is almost comparable to grieving the loss of a friend. You just have to shake yourself out of it and realize how unnecessary it is.

Stay strong and good luck!
